title: streaming-lifecycle-controls-reconnect-resume-server-timeouts-openai-compat
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle: more robust client-cancel handling, deterministic disconnect/reconnect resume behavior, and configurable server-side stream timeouts. Backwards-compatible OpenAI-compat streaming semantics preserved.
description: Motivation: downstream clients (web SDKs, mobile apps, and third-party OpenAI-compat wrappers) have experienced inconsistent outcomes when a client cancels a stream, disconnects, or attempts to reconnect. Symptoms included duplicate partial events, leaked KV-cache state, and confusing finalization events in the OpenAI-compatible streaming layer. This PR consolidates lifecycle handling across the serving runtime and the OpenAI-compat gateway to make outcomes deterministic and recoverable. What changed: 1) Client-cancel handling: introduce an explicit CANCEL message that short-circuits generation, flushes partial tokens, and emits a single terminal event. 2) Disconnect/reconnect: add resumable stream tokens tied to in-memory (and persisted for Private/Dedicated) stream state with an expiration window. Reconnect attempts within the window will resume from the last acknowledged token; out-of-window reconnects will gracefully restart. 3) Server timeouts: add configurable server-side idle and generation timeouts with clearer error payloads and automatic checkpointing for resumable streams. 4) OpenAI compatibility: keep the same event shapes as the compatibility layer (data: {"delta": ...}, [DONE]) while adding an optional resume token field in `meta` for downstream SDKs that opt-in. 5) Observability and tracing: emit lifecycle events (cancel_received, stream_checkpointed, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_expired, timeout_terminated) to tracing and metrics. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for clients that do not use resume tokens; resume is opt-in via `Resume-Allowed: true` header or resume_enabled flag in the SDK. Implementation notes: changes span the serving runtime (stream manager and KV cache guard), the OpenAI-compat gateway (stream mux and event serializer), and the Python/TS SDKs (resume token helpers and reconnection utilities). Tests: end-to-end functional tests covering cancel + reconnect races, unit tests for stream state transitions, and load tests for the resume token lookup path. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `streaming_resume_v2` with a gradual rollout on Hosted and Dedicated; Private installs can opt into the feature in the installer. Related: ENG-1789 (stream lifecycle stabilization), SUP-4123 (customer report: reconnect causing duplicate content).
commits: 3 commits: (1) core: stream manager: add resume token lifecycle & expiration + checkpoint persistence; (2) compat: openai-gateway: add resume token metadata and updated event serializer; (3) sdk: python & ts: add helper to exchange resume tokens and retry reconnects with exponential backoff; plus assorted test and docs updates.
patch_snippets: stream_manager.rs: add StreamState::Checkpointed with resume_token and expires_at; handle Cancel -> emit terminal and release kv-cache
serializer.go: include meta.resume_token when resume_allowed header is present; keep data/delta/DONE shapes unchanged
resume.ts: expose getResumeToken() and reconnectWithResume(token) helpers
review_comments: Eric Patel: Please add a unit test for concurrent cancel+ack races; ensure KV cache release is idempotent.
Maya Chen (author): Added tests in stream_manager_test.rs covering 3 race scenarios and made kv_cache_guard.release idempotent.
Ravi Kapoor: The resume token persistence path looks hot under load; can we memoize lookups? Consider a small LRU cache.
Maya Chen: Added a small in-memory LRU for hosted path and a metrics counter. Load tests show <5% tail latency increase at 500 qps for resume lookups.
Leah Gomez: Docs look good. One nit: call out default resume TTL in the public API reference.
Maya Chen: Updated docs and public API reference with resume TTL and example flow.
qa_notes: E2E checklist: 1) cancel during generation -> single terminal event; 2) disconnect then reconnect within TTL -> resume from last acked token; 3) reconnect after TTL -> new generation but graceful error payload for client; 4) heavy load: resume token lookup path should not exceed 50ms p95; 5) OpenAI-compat clients that don't set resume header should be unaffected.
Test harness: added new harness scenarios in perf-canary to simulate flaky mobile network reconnects.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged `streaming_resume_v2`. Rollout: 10% host traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with canary checks on error rate, latency p95, and resume success rate. Dedicated customers will be offered opt-in windows and operator docs. Private installer includes an upgrade flag to enable resume behavior.
notes_for_ops: If customers report resume failures, check resume_token store TTL and LRU evictions; metric `stream.resume.expired` will indicate systemic TTL mismatches. If duplicate tokens observed, enable debug logging for stream_id and resume_token for a short window.
examples: Python SDK: client.start_stream(resume_allowed=True) -> on_disconnect: client.get_resume_token() -> client.reconnect_with_resume(token)
OpenAI-compat: add header Resume-Allowed: true; gateway emits meta.resume_token in first event
